candidate.answerReason: Each removed unit corner cube eliminates three exposed unit squares and exposes three previously internal unit squares. The surface area remains 6 × 3² = 54 square centimeters.

methods.label: Compare the area lost and exposed
methods.explanation:
Removing a corner cube takes away some outside surface, but it also exposes new surface. Tracking both changes makes it unnecessary to count every face of the finished solid.

The figure divides each \(3\text{ cm}\) edge into three equal parts, so each small cube has side length \(1\text{ cm}\). At a corner, three faces of that small cube lie on the original outside surface. Removing it eliminates those three \(1\text{ cm}^2\) squares and exposes three new \(1\text{ cm}^2\) squares on the neighboring cubes. Thus the net change is
\[
-3+3=0\text{ cm}^2.
\]
No two corner cubes share a face, so these replacements remain valid when all eight corner cubes are removed. The surface area consequently equals that of the original cube:
\[
6\cdot3^2=\boxed{54\text{ cm}^2},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: The preservation argument is a direct comparison of equal square areas, requiring only elementary cube geometry and arithmetic.

methods.label: Count the remaining and newly exposed squares
methods.explanation:
Separate the finished surface into squares left on the original faces and squares newly exposed by the removals. Each small cube in the figure has side length \(1\text{ cm}\), so every small square has area \(1\text{ cm}^2\).

Each original face contains \(9\) small squares. Removing its four corner cubes leaves \(9-4=5\) squares on that face. Across the six original faces, this contributes \(6\cdot5=30\text{ cm}^2\).

Each of the eight removed corner cubes also exposes three new unit squares. No two corner cubes share a face, so all \(8\cdot3=24\) of these squares are distinct and remain exposed. Every surface square is either on an original face or was exposed by a removal, and none belongs to both groups. Hence the total surface area is
\[
30+24=\boxed{54\text{ cm}^2},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method counts unit square faces in two disjoint groups and uses only elementary spatial reasoning and arithmetic.
